hero.label: Welcome
hero.title: Capoeira4Life
hero.lead: Capoeira, culture and community in the heart of London.
body: Capoeira4Life is the Capoeira Nagô project in London, dedicated to bringing people of all ages closer to capoeira through classes, music, movement and roda.
We train adults and children at Moberly Sports Centre in Kensal Rise, with experienced coaches and deep respect for the Afro-Brazilian roots of the art.

academy.label: The Academy
academy.title: Moberly Sports Centre
academy.subtitle: Our main home in London is Moberly Sports Centre in the heart of Kensal Rise.
academy.lead: Our home in London is Moberly Sports Centre: a spacious, welcoming and well-equipped gym where we train capoeira every week.
body: Adult capoeira, Capoeirinha and open training sessions all happen here, in a dedicated hall with room for ginga, sequences, music and roda. It is the meeting point for our London community.
The centre is easy to reach, with good transport links and facilities for students of all ages. Wear comfortable clothes, bring water and come discover our roda.
Want to try it? Book a class or drop in at one of the times below. We look forward to welcoming you at the academy.

about.title: About Capoeira4Life
about.valuesText: Respect for Afro-Brazilian roots, inclusion in the roda, discipline with joy, and community above all.
about.missionText: To bring capoeira to everyone, training complete capoeiristas and preserving the culture with specialized masters.
about.visionText: To be a reference in capoeira, uniting tradition and innovation, in London and beyond.

nago.label: Our group
nago.title: Capoeira Nagô
nago.lead: Preserving Afro-Brazilian traditions and taking capoeira to the world since 2002.
nago.body: Founded in Goiânia by Mestre Pequinês with support from Mestre Suíno, Capoeira Nagô Sports Association honours the Yoruba roots of the art. The name "Nagô" references the African peoples who shaped capoeira in Brazil. Today the group is present across Brazil and internationally, balancing high-performance sport with music, mutual respect and social inclusion.

founder.label: Founder
founder.name: Mestre Pequinês
founder.text: Mestre Pequinês founded Capoeira Nagô in 2002 with a mission to keep ancestral roots alive while transforming lives through capoeira. He also created Elite Capoeira Fight, a system of automatically matched capoeira bouts that combines competition, technique and respect for tradition.

cords.label: Graduation
cords.title: Belt Exchange
cords.lead: In capoeira, a student's progress is marked by belts that symbolise level of knowledge, responsibility and dedication to the art.
body: Unlike other martial arts, capoeira uses coloured belts (cordas). Each colour represents a stage on the capoeirista's journey, from beginner student to master. In Capoeira Nagô, the official system includes specific paths for adults, children (5 to 10 years) and youth (11 to 14 years), as shown in the chart.

A belt exchange is not based on training time alone. The master or teacher evaluates technical growth, musicality, knowledge of history and rituals, behaviour inside and outside the roda, and respect for tradition. Each student progresses at their own pace.

The exchange ceremony is both festive and solemn: family, friends and the whole roda come together. The capoeirista plays, sings and demonstrates what they have learned. Receiving a new belt also means taking on new responsibilities within the group.

steps.title: Ceremony in the roda
steps.text: The new belt is given at a collective event, with games, songs and community celebration.

intro.label: Capoeira4Life Project
intro.title: O Capoeirinha
intro.lead: Capoeira for the little ones: fun, movement and culture from an early age.
intro.body: O Capoeirinha is a Capoeira4Life initiative created to introduce children to capoeira in a playful, safe and inspiring way. Through games, music and movement, kids learn coordination, respect, confidence and the rich cultural roots of this Brazilian art, all while having fun.

about.label: The project
about.title: Meet O Capoeirinha
about.avatarText: O Capoeirinha is our friendly mascot: a young capoeirista who guides children through every move, making learning feel like an adventure. Colourful, energetic and full of personality, he represents the joy and freedom that capoeira brings to kids.

features.title: Safe & adapted
features.text: Movements designed for each age group, with guidance and care at every step.

features.title: Brazilian culture

moves.label: Learn
moves.title: Capoeira Moves
moves.subtitle: Swipe through the moves and learn with O Capoeirinha

items.name: Ginga
items.description: The base movement of capoeira: a rhythmic sway from side to side that teaches balance, flow and readiness for any move.

items.name: Cocorinha
items.description: A crouching defence: we bend the knees and stay low, one hand on the ground, ready to protect ourselves and spring back up.

items.name: Martelo
items.description: A strong kick that rises from the side like a hammer. Works balance, leg strength and aim.

items.name: Queixada
items.description: A crescent kick that slices through the air from the inside out. Teaches hip opening, coordination and lightness.

items.name: Au
items.description: A cartwheel performed with open arms. It develops coordination, spatial awareness and the courage to move freely.

items.name: Macaquinho
items.description: A low move close to the ground, like a little monkey. Builds agility, arm strength and playful movement.

items.name: Ponte
items.description: A bridge with the body arched upward. Strengthens arms, legs and spine. A fun challenge for the little ones!

graduation.label: Graduations
graduation.title: Belts for Children & Teens
graduation.lead: Graduation in Capoeirinha celebrates effort, technical growth and respect for capoeira culture.
body: Children and teenagers earn belts as they progress in class. Each colour marks a stage of learning, from first steps to more advanced movements.
Evaluations consider participation, respect, musicality and mastery of fundamentals, not just physical ability. Every child grows at their own pace.
Teens follow a progressive path that prepares them for the adult graduation system, keeping the same values of discipline and cultural identity.

steps.title: Progressive evolution
steps.text: Each belt represents a new challenge conquered with dedication in class.

steps.title: Fair criteria
steps.text: Behaviour, attendance and love for capoeira count as much as technique.

steps.title: Celebration ritual
steps.text: Graduation ceremonies are festive moments with family, friends and the whole roda.

history.label: History
history.title: Capoeira
history.lead: A martial art, dance and culture born from the resistance of African peoples in Brazil.
paragraphs: Created during the colonial period as a form of physical and cultural resistance, capoeira was born among enslaved African peoples in Brazil, especially in Bahia. On the plantations and in quilombos, strikes, escapes and acrobatics were disguised with music, dance and rhythm to evade the surveillance of slave owners.

After abolition in 1888, the practice was criminalised and persecuted in the cities. Even so, it survived in the streets, terreiros and rodas, preserving the berimbau, atabaque, pandeiro and the songs that still guide the game today.

In the 1930s, capoeira gained institutional recognition: Mestre Bimba structured Capoeira Regional and Mestre Pastinha consolidated Capoeira Angola. In 2014, UNESCO recognised the Capoeira Circle as Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity, and today it is practised worldwide as an expression of fight, art and community.

classes.label: In class
classes.title: What capoeira classes are like
classes.lead: Movement, music and community in every session
paragraphs: In Capoeira4Life classes you get ginga, sequences, music and the roda in the same space. We start with a warm-up and fundamentals, move into techniques and combinations, and finish by playing, singing and training together.
The training suits every level. Beginners learn at their own pace, with clear guidance from the coaches. Experienced players find challenge, musicality and steady progress.
More than technique, the classes are about community. Respect, energy and Afro-Brazilian culture shape every session, so adults and children feel part of the roda from day one.

fabricio.name: Mestre Fabricio
paragraphs: A leading figure in Capoeira Nagô, Fabricio brings decades of practice, teaching and event organisation. Born in Goiânia, he discovered capoeira as a child and turned that passion into structured programmes for children and adults, blending technique, musicality and cultural identity.

With the experience of someone who has lived the art in competitions, performances and international rodas, he shares capoeira as fighting, dance and acrobatics in one flow. Watching students grow in confidence, strength and resilience is the greatest reward.
achievements: Master title, highest rank, awarded in Brazil in 2019
Founder of Capoeira Nagô Academy in Rome, Italy
Central judge at international capoeira competitions

samurai.name: Coach Samurai
samurai.imageAlt: Coach Pablo Samurai Conti, director of Capoeira4Life
paragraphs: From Goiânia, Pablo "Samurai" Conti built his path through rigorous training and deep respect for Afro-Brazilian roots. A coach and director at Capoeira4Life, he brings energy and precision to every class and roda.

He has travelled across Europe sharing the rhythm, movement and philosophy of capoeira. Known as an ambassador of Brazilian culture, he preserves tradition while inspiring new generations of practitioners.

esquilo.name: Coach Esquilo
paragraphs: David Ok, known as Esquilo, combines martial arts, teaching and science. Born in Paris, he has practised capoeira since 2016, but before that spent over 20 years in judo, reaching 1st dan black belt.

Since 2021 he has coached capoeira for children aged 5 to 10, bringing the patience and method of someone who has also taught classical guitar and computer science. Outside the roda, he is an AI scientist with a PhD in computer vision.
achievements: 1st place UK Solta o Jogo 2023 (advanced team)

coqueiro.name: Coach Coqueiro
paragraphs: Emanuel Silva, Coqueiro, brings a strong background in sport and education. Born in Cape Verde, he grew up between Portugal and England, where he graduated with a BSc in Sport Science (Teaching & Coaching).

Since 2013 he has coached children from 18 months to 12 years old, and has trained capoeira for around 7 years. He blends energy, pedagogy and care for every student, in capoeira classes and as a Level 3 personal trainer.
achievements: 1st place UK Solta o Jogo 2023 (advanced team)

masters.label: Legacy
masters.title: Pioneer Masters
masters.bimbaText: Mestre Bimba revolutionised the art by creating Capoeira Regional in the 1930s. He transformed the practice into a disciplined method of self-defence, introducing white uniforms, strict rules and the first teaching methodology. In 1937, after performing for President Getúlio Vargas, he legalised capoeira as a national sport. His style is marked by a fast, upright, athletic game focused on the efficiency of strikes.
masters.bimbaImageAlt: Mestre Bimba, creator of Capoeira Regional
masters.pastinhaText: Mestre Pastinha became the great guardian of Capoeira Angola, the traditional style. In 1941, he founded his official school to preserve the African roots, ritual and philosophy of the art. He believed capoeira was a dance of cunning and strategy, played more slowly, rhythmically and close to the ground. He also standardised his students' uniforms in black and yellow.

agogo.title: Agogô
agogo.description: The double bell that locks in the bateria's pulse. Clear tone and strong presence in the roda — great for class and music practice.

atabaque.title: Atabaque
atabaque.description: The heartbeat of the capoeira orchestra. Handcrafted with a natural skin head to carry the roda's rhythms with power and tradition.

berimbau.title: Berimbau
berimbau.description: Capoeira's iconic leading instrument. Available as gunga, médio and viola to guide the game with the right toque every time.

pandeiro.title: Pandeiro
pandeiro.description: Light, responsive and essential in the bateria. Supports berimbau and atabaque with groove and precision in training and in the roda.

tenis.title: Capoeira trainers
tenis.description: Built for ginga, falls and quick base changes. Grip and comfort so you can train safely in class and in the roda.

dnv-cultural-2026.title: DNA Cultural 2026
dnv-cultural-2026.description: A new Capoeira Nagô gathering in London, for adults and children, introducing Capoeirinha Nagô Kids UK.

capoeirinha.headline: Our new mascot has arrived
capoeirinha.lead: Look who's here to brighten up our roda: O Capoeirinha, the new mascot of Capoeira Nagô Kids UK! Cheerful, strong and full of energy.
body: O Capoeirinha is the face of our energy: a young capoeirista full of movement, inviting children to discover capoeira with joy, music and play.
Come and be part of this magical world, meet the mascot up close and grab a photo with him. You're our special guest!
An initiative by Professor Samurai, within the Capoeira Nagô Kids UK project in London, to bring the little ones closer to capoeira from an early age.

dnv-cultural-2025.headline: Contramestre Fumaça in the London roda
dnv-cultural-2025.lead: At DNA Cultural 2025, Capoeira4Life welcomed Contramestre Fumaça from Germany for a special workshop in London.
body: The theme was "Legacy of my master": an afternoon of capoeira with technique, musicality and plenty of roda, bringing the experience of one of Capoeira Nagô's leading names in Europe.
The event was organised by Professor Samurai and supervised by Mestre Fabricio, bringing capoeiristas of different levels together in a shared space of learning and celebration.
Beyond the workshop, the gathering included roda, community time and memories that show the strength of our London community. An edition to train, play and share the Nagô tradition.
It was an important moment for Capoeira4Life: welcoming a guest of stature, exchanging knowledge and strengthening the bond between masters, coaches and students within the DNA Cultural project.

dnv-cultural-2026.headline: Your identity in the roda
dnv-cultural-2026.lead: On 23 and 24 October 2026, Capoeira4Life presents DNA Cultural: two days of capoeira in London, for adults and children, celebrating the identity and roots of Capoeira Nagô.
body: An edition designed for the whole community: adults and children train, play and share the roda, with workshops, musicality and plenty of knowledge exchange.
We will also introduce Capoeirinha Nagô Kids UK, the mascot created to bring children closer to capoeira with joy and purpose, making every class more fun and inspiring.
The event is organised by Professor Samurai and supervised by Mestre Fabricio, bringing masters, coaches and students together in one space of celebration.
Mark your calendar: 23 and 24 October. It will be a weekend to live the Nagô identity in and out of the roda.
